problem: For the function $f(x,y,z)=z-4{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}+1,$ find the equation of the level surface $f(x,y,z)=1.$

feedback.problem: For the function $f(x,y,z)={e}^{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-z-1},$ find the equation of the level surface $f(x,y,z)=1.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The level surfaces for the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the equation

$$
f(x,y,z)=c.
$$

In our case, we're interested in $c=1.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =c \\ {e}^{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-z-1} & =1 \\ {x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-z-1 & =0 \\ z & ={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the level surface for $c=1$ is the paraboloid $z={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-1.$
